subject: Re: Order form — proposed cap/floor delta-offset and worksheet
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rivas <elena@bluehorizon.ai>, procurement@bluehorizon.ai
Cc: 
Date: 2027-04-24T08:41:00-07:00
Subject: Initial: order form redlines — caps & floors worksheet

Hi Elena / Blue Horizon procurement team,

Thanks for the redlines on the order form. We reviewed the exhibit and wanted to propose an alternative that addresses your concern about downside rigidity while protecting Redwood's economics in high-burst scenarios. Attached is a short worksheet (BH-Proposed-Pricing-Schedule-v2.xlsx) that shows the numbers and a sample annual true-up.

High level: instead of a fixed-dollar floor, we'd like to propose a delta-offset mechanism — a percentage-based floor tied to the committed monthly token slab with an asymmetric true-up at year-end (see tab "Delta Offset"). The intent is to: 
- give Blue Horizon downside protection if actual usage falls short of commit in year 1,
- apply a modest surcharge smoothing ramp over Q1/Q2 to avoid a large one-time true-up, and
- preserve a hard cap per-token for burst traffic above the committed band.

Could you confirm whether a percentage floor and a 90-day smoothing window would be acceptable, or if you prefer a fixed-dollar minimum? If percentage floor is ok, we'll convert the worksheet into redline language for the order form.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments: BH-Proposed-Pricing-Schedule-v2.xlsx

From: Elena Rivas <elena@bluehorizon.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, ben.carter@bluehorizon.ai, procurement@bluehorizon.ai
Cc: 
Date: 2027-04-24T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: order form redlines — caps & floors worksheet

Soojin,

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the workbook. The team here is generally supportive of a percentage-based approach versus a hard dollar floor, but two asks before we can sign off: 

1) Show a worked example where actual usage is 55% of committed in Year 1 and how the smoothing ramp would apply (we want to avoid a large retro true-up hitting our Q4).
2) Can you add a clause that the floor calculation excludes trial/dev/test buckets and internal eval projects (we will provide a list of project IDs)?

Also, procurement would like any automatic surcharge to be capped at 3% per month during the smoothing window. If you can add that cap to the worksheet and the redline language, procurement will route internally (legal + CFO).

Thanks,
Elena Rivas
Head of Procurement, Blue Horizon AI
elena@bluehorizon.ai

Attachment: OrderForm-Redline-20270424.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-04-24T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: order form redlines — Blue Horizon asks (worked example + exclusion list + 3% monthly cap)

FYI — Blue Horizon is ok with the percentage-floor idea but asked for three specific items in the redline: 
1) worked example where actual usage = 55% of commit, show smoothing ramp,
2) explicit exclusion for dev/test/trial project IDs,
3) cap the monthly smoothing surcharge at 3%.

Can Legal/Product weigh in on whether (a) the delta-offset formula below is defensible, and (b) we can draft precise contract language for the exclusions? I've attached their redline PDF for context.

Quick proposed formula (from worksheet):
- Floor = max(CommittedMonthly * FloorPct, MinFloorAbsolute)
- Monthly surcharge during smoothing = min(3% * PrevMonthInvoice, CalculatedSurcharge)
- Year-end true-up = sum(Committed - ActualUsageAdjustedForExclusions) * TokenRate * TrueUpMultiplier

I'll add a sample calc sheet but please flag any legal/regulatory issues (tax treatment, GAAP recognition we'll need to note?)

Thanks,
Soojin

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-04-25T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: order form redlines — Blue Horizon asks (worked example + exclusion list + 3% monthly cap)

Soojin / team,

Thanks for looping us in. Legal has reviewed the worksheet and we're comfortable with a percentage-based floor provided the following clarifications are incorporated into the exhibit: 

1) Define "Eligible Usage" and "Excluded Usage" precisely (project IDs + explicit prefixes for sandbox/test). Exclusions must be auditable — procurement will provide the list quarterly.
2) The smoothing cap of 3% per month is acceptable, but it must be expressed as a cap on the "monthly adjustment" line item and applied before any invoice rounding. 
3) For the true-up formula, replace the vague "TrueUpMultiplier" with a fixed scalar: 1.0 for Year 1, 0.75 for Year 2 (if renewal), to reflect ramp risks.

Worked example (55% actual vs commit) — concise numbers: 
- Committed monthly tokens: 10,000,000
- FloorPct proposed: 65% -> Floor tokens = 6,500,000 equivalent
- Actual eligible usage (excl. trials): 5,500,000 (55%)
- Monthly shortfall for true-up in month M = max(0, Floor tokens - Actual eligible usage M)
- With 90-day smoothing: surcharge applied across next 3 invoices, but capped at 3% per invoice, resulting cumulative collection of ~X% (see attached calc).

We'll draft redline language to: (i) set FloorPct numeric default (65%) with a MinimumDollarFloor of $5,000 for Year 1, (ii) add audit/exclusion process, (iii) state 90-day smoothing window and 3% monthly cap.

If marketing/legal wants a more conservative FloorPct we can lower it; otherwise I think this is a pragmatic path forward.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts & GTM
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T10:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: order form redlines — Blue Horizon asks (worked example + exclusion list + 3% monthly cap)

Agree with Marissa. A couple of commercial notes: 
- Preserve the SLA-trigger language so that if Blue Horizon goes above the committed band by >25% for 3 consecutive months, they automatically fall into the burst rate (protects us on sustained overage).
- For billing ops: we need procurement to deliver the exclusion list at least 10 business days before quarter close or we cannot retroactively adjust prior invoices. Please make that explicit in the exhibit.

From a negotiation standpoint, offering a $5k minimum for Year 1 + 65% FloorPct should be an easy sell. Would advise Soojin to propose a one-time onboarding credit of $2,000 if they provide their exclusion list within 30 days (good faith gesture).

Ben Carter
Director, Sales Operations
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Elena Rivas <elena@bluehorizon.ai>

Soojin / Marissa / Ben,

Thanks — this addresses our concerns. Blue Horizon accepts the percentage-floor approach with the following confirmations: 
1) FloorPct = 65% for Year 1 with a MinimumDollarFloor = $5,000,
2) Exclusions will be a quarterly auditable list; procurement will deliver the first list within 21 days to qualify for an onboarding credit,
3) Monthly smoothing surcharge capped at 3% per invoice for a 90-day window,
4) SLA-trigger and burst-rate protection acknowledged.

Please send the updated redline (Order Form exhibit) and a DocuSign package and we'll route it for signature. We expect to have final sign-off from CFO within 5 business days after we see the DocuSign package.

Elena
